gaps.concept: Chlamydial cervicitis causes mucopurulent discharge, cervical friability, and postcoital bleeding; infection is often asymptomatic.
gaps.why_tested: A sexually active patient has a friable cervix and positive chlamydial NAAT despite few symptoms.

gaps.concept: Chlamydial urethritis can cause dysuria and pyuria without organisms on Gram stain or routine urine culture.
gaps.why_tested: A patient has urethral symptoms, white cells in urine, and a negative routine culture.

gaps.concept: C. trachomatis forms glycogen-containing intracytoplasmic inclusions visible with iodine or Giemsa stain.
gaps.why_tested: A cytology or microscopy image shows inclusions in infected epithelial cells.

gaps.concept: Gonorrhea commonly causes purulent urethral discharge in men; cervical infection in women may be asymptomatic.
gaps.why_tested: A stem contrasts a symptomatic male partner with a female partner who has few symptoms.

gaps.concept: N. gonorrhoeae is oxidase positive, ferments glucose but not maltose, and grows on selective Thayer-Martin medium.
gaps.why_tested: Culture and biochemical results distinguish gonococcus from other Neisseria species.

gaps.concept: NAAT is the preferred diagnostic test for uncomplicated genital gonorrhea; culture permits antimicrobial susceptibility testing.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks which test diagnoses infection or investigates suspected antibiotic resistance.

gaps.concept: Gonococcal lipooligosaccharide drives inflammation and lacks the long O-antigen chains of typical lipopolysaccharide.
gaps.why_tested: A mechanism question links gonococcal mucosal infection to endotoxin-mediated inflammation.

gaps.concept: Gonorrhea and chlamydia frequently coexist; add doxycycline to gonorrhea treatment when chlamydia has not been excluded.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with confirmed gonorrhea has no chlamydia result, and the question asks for initial therapy.

gaps.concept: Gonococcal ophthalmia typically appears 2–5 days after birth with copious pus; chlamydial conjunctivitis usually appears after 5 days.
gaps.why_tested: An infant’s age and ocular discharge distinguish the causes of neonatal conjunctivitis.

gaps.concept: Chlamydial or gonococcal epididymitis causes gradual unilateral scrotal pain and swelling, often with concurrent urethritis.
gaps.why_tested: A sexually active young man has epididymal tenderness and a positive STI test.

gaps.concept: M. genitalium lacks a cell wall, resists beta-lactams, and is associated with persistent urethritis, cervicitis, and PID.
gaps.why_tested: Urethritis persists after usual therapy, or a drug-mechanism question asks why penicillin fails.

gaps.concept: T. pallidum is a thin motile spirochete poorly seen on Gram stain; silver stain can reveal organisms in tissue.
gaps.why_tested: A lesion specimen shows spiral organisms on darkfield or silver stain despite an unrevealing Gram stain.

gaps.concept: Syphilitic lesions characteristically show plasma cell infiltrates and obliterative endarteritis.
gaps.why_tested: A biopsy asks for the characteristic inflammatory cells or vascular lesion.

gaps.concept: Syphilitic aortitis results from obliterative endarteritis of the vasa vasorum and can cause ascending aneurysm or aortic regurgitation.
gaps.why_tested: A late-syphilis stem asks for the mechanism of thoracic aortic disease.

gaps.concept: RPR and VDRL detect anticardiolipin antibodies; titers track disease activity, whereas treponemal tests generally remain positive after treatment.
gaps.why_tested: A previously treated patient has persistent treponemal positivity but falling nontreponemal titers.

gaps.concept: Very high antibody concentrations can cause a false-negative RPR or VDRL through the prozone effect; dilution restores reactivity.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with convincing secondary syphilis has an unexpectedly negative screening test.

gaps.concept: Reactive CSF-VDRL is highly specific for neurosyphilis but is insufficiently sensitive to exclude it when negative.
gaps.why_tested: Neurologic symptoms and serum syphilis tests conflict with a negative cerebrospinal fluid test.

gaps.concept: Congenital syphilis crosses the placenta and may cause stillbirth, snuffles, rash, hepatosplenomegaly, and long-bone abnormalities.
gaps.why_tested: An infant of an untreated mother has persistent rhinitis and abnormal long-bone radiographs.

gaps.concept: Late congenital syphilis causes Hutchinson teeth, interstitial keratitis, and sensorineural hearing loss.
gaps.why_tested: A child with notched incisors and hearing loss is linked to maternal infection.

gaps.concept: Penicillin G is required for syphilis in pregnancy; patients with penicillin allergy require desensitization to prevent congenital infection.
gaps.why_tested: A pregnant patient with syphilis reports penicillin allergy, and the question asks for effective therapy.

gaps.concept: Acute PID produces neutrophilic salpingitis and may form a pus-filled tube (pyosalpinx); chronic scarring can cause hydrosalpinx.
gaps.why_tested: A tubal specimen or imaging study shows pus or a dilated fluid-filled tube after PID.

gaps.concept: Transvaginal ultrasound findings supporting PID include thickened, fluid-filled fallopian tubes and a tubo-ovarian complex.
gaps.why_tested: Pelvic pain and cervical tenderness are paired with an imaging finding to identify PID.

gaps.concept: PID can be present without fever or a positive gonorrhea or chlamydia test.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with pelvic pain and cervical motion tenderness has normal temperature and negative cervical STI tests.

gaps.concept: Sexually transmitted LGV is caused by invasive C. trachomatis serovars L1–L3 and is treated with doxycycline.
gaps.why_tested: A transient genital lesion precedes painful inguinal lymphadenopathy, and the question asks for organism classification or therapy.

gaps.concept: Azithromycin is a first-line treatment option for chancroid and granuloma inguinale.
gaps.why_tested: An ulcer vignette identifies either organism and asks for an appropriate antibiotic.
